summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a two-day history of productive cough and shortness of breath unresponsive to inhaler therapy. She was treated in the emergency department with oxygen, nebulizers, intravenous steroids, and antibiotics. Her symptoms were attributed to a combination of asthma exacerbation and acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, supported by elevated BNP and radiographic findings. She responded well to diuresis and respiratory support, was weaned off oxygen, and improved clinically. A urine culture from an outpatient visit revealed Enterobacter cloacae, and she was discharged on a 7-day course of ciprofloxacin. Her warfarin dose was increased to 5 mg daily due to subtherapeutic INR, with instructions to monitor INR during antibiotic use. She was restarted on her home medications, including furosemide and inhalers, and advised on fluid and sodium restriction, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up care.
